skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Perform Sentry-style code reviews for pull requests and code changes. Focus on security, performance, tests, design, and maintainable feedback.
skill.summary: Review code changes with a structured Sentry engineering checklist.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown-only code review checklist and does not contain executable scripts. All static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, educational examples, and a reference link.

static_findings.snippet: Verify tests cover actual requirements and edge cases. Avoid excessive branching or looping in test
- **Runtime errors**: Potential exceptions, null pointer issues, out-of-bounds access

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 67 starts a Markdown Python code fence for a review example. It does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or backtick command substitution.
Line 74 closes a Markdown code fence. It is documentation syntax and provides no executable command path.
Line 78 starts a Markdown TypeScript code fence for a React review example. The skill contains no mechanism to run that content.
Line 88 closes a Markdown code fence. It is not a shell backtick execution pattern in operational code.
Line 92 starts a Markdown Python code fence for a SQL injection example. The example is educational and is not executed by the skill.
The URL is a documentation reference to Sentry code review guidance. The skill does not instruct the agent to fetch it or transmit data.
The line advises checking test coverage and avoiding overly complex tests. It does not request host, process, network, or environment reconnaissance.
The line shows a bad SQL query as a vulnerability example. It is static review guidance and not an instruction to inspect the host system.
The line shows a parameterized SQL query as the safe alternative. It is documentation content and has no system reconnaissance behavior.
The line lists runtime error classes to consider during review. It does not direct network probing or collection of network information.

content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, performance, and testing issues. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured Sentry-style review checklist.
actual_capabilities: Identifies runtime errors, performance risks, side effects, and compatibility concerns in code changes.
Checks security risks such as injection, cross-site scripting, access control gaps, and secrets exposure.
Reviews test coverage for business logic, integrations, and critical user paths.
Assesses design fit against existing architecture and component interactions.
Guides review comments toward polite, actionable, and risk-focused feedback.
limitations: It does not run tests, static analyzers, or security scanners by itself.
It reflects Sentry-style practices and may need adaptation for other teams.
It needs relevant diffs, requirements, or project context for accurate feedback.
It cannot replace senior review for high-risk architecture or security changes.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply a structured checklist to find defects, missing tests, and design concerns before approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Convert review observations into polite, specific comments that explain risk and suggest next steps.

use_cases.title: Screen Risky Changes
use_cases.description: Flag database, API, framework, performance, or security changes that may need senior review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Code Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request using the Sentry code review checklist. Focus on defects, tests, and clear feedback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first pass on a small or routine code change.

prompt_templates.title: Security and Performance Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff for security vulnerabilities, performance risks, and missing safeguards. Explain each issue and suggest a fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the change touches data handling, authentication, queries, or hot paths.

prompt_templates.title: Design Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this change for architecture fit, component interactions, API compatibility, and long-term maintenance impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a change affects shared interfaces or core system structure.

prompt_templates.title: Senior Review Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this change should be escalated for senior review. Consider schema changes, API contracts, frameworks, performance, and security.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before approving a high-impact pull request.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a new data query and updates a React effect.
output: Flags a possible query performance issue and asks for prefetching or batching.
Notes a missing effect dependency that can create stale data.
Requests focused tests for the changed behavior and edge cases.

output_examples.input: A reviewer needs feedback for a security-sensitive database change.
output: Identifies injection and access control concerns in plain language.
Suggests parameterized queries and permission checks.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants a concise approval summary for a low-risk change.
output_examples.output: Provides a short risk summary, lists any remaining minor issues, and explains why the change can be approved.

best_practices: Provide the diff, linked requirements, and relevant project conventions before asking for review.
Ask for separate passes when security, performance, or architecture risk is high.
Use the feedback as review support, then verify important findings with local tests or tools.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to approve changes without showing the relevant code context.
Do not treat checklist output as a replacement for required owner review.
Do not ignore project-specific standards when they conflict with generic guidance.

faq.question: What kind of code review does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports pull request and code change review with attention to defects, tests, design, security, and performance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code or run tests?
faq.answer: No. It gives review guidance and feedback based on the code and context you provide.

faq.question: Can it review non-Sentry projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The checklist is general enough for many projects, but teams should add their own standards.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the diff, intended behavior, related requirements, test changes, and any known risk areas.

faq.question: When should I escalate to a senior reviewer?
faq.answer: Escalate when changes affect schemas, API contracts, new frameworks, performance-critical paths, or security-sensitive code.
